newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's trade deficit improved in Jan-July 1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's trade deficit improved in Jan-July 1996.

text.p: Morocco's trade deficit fell by nearly two percent in the first seven months of 1996 compared with the same period last year, due to the stability of global commercial transactions, the official Office des Changes said.

The gap between imports and exports in the period was 15.3 billion dirhams compared with 15.6 billion dirhams or a slight decline of 1.9 percent, the Office des Changes regulatory body said on Thursday in its monthly report.
Morocco imported in value 48.1 billion dirhams in the period of January-July 1996 compared with 48.4 billion dirhams in the same period 1995.
Exports remained stable at 32.8 billion dirhams in the first seven months of the year compared with the previous period.

To comply with the International Monetary Fund trade rules, the Office des Change said "it included, (for the first time) in its calculation of the global transactions, the imported goods without payment and re-exported after transformation."
Moroccans living abroad remitted 10.1 billion dirhams, up 5.8 percent in the period compared with the seven months of 1995.
Tourism receipts improved by 20.5 percent to 6.4 billion dirhams in the period of January-July 1996 compared with the first seven months of 1995.
The office said investments and foreign private loans dropped 32 percent to 1.6 billion dirhams in the seven months of the year compared with the same period last year.
